title: The Fossil Record Becoming Conscious

features.name: shell half-emerged from stone
features.desc-on-touch: you can see both the ocean and the earth that swallowed it. 40 million years compressed into one inch of sediment. you feel the weight of every year, every season, every tide that contributed to this.

features.name: the excavation marks
features.desc-on-touch: chisel-lines and grid-marks in pencil, never erased, dating back decades. each archaeologist left their fingerprint by measuring. the stone keeps every touch.

features.name: an eye descending into the strata
features.desc-on-touch: downward gaze into laminations of clay and sandstone. each layer a year, each year a layer. the eye learns to read backwards in time the way you read text, letter by letter, layer by layer.

features.name: dated stone with unknown genus
features.desc-on-touch: radiometric tags affirm the age, but the creature itself remains unnamed. it lived once, was buried, was discovered, was measured, was filed. now it is conscious of none of those things except through your reading.

features.name: the repeated pattern in the stone
features.desc-on-touch: microfossils in rows, same creature, same depth, but with slight variations. evolution captured mid-blink. the repetition is not exact—which suggests the stone itself is learning.

inscription: you are holding the moment when the ocean stopped being a sea and became a memory in rock

reverie.title: REVERIE — holding the ocean on your palm
narr: she kneels at the dig and pulls back the dust carefully.
her hand trembles. you see it: a shell, small, spiraled,
still curved the way it curled 40 million years ago.
she turns it over and you hold your palm beneath hers.
together you hold the weight of every ocean that has existed
in the compass of something smaller than a fingernail.
